mutations.before: where m.user_id = $1 and o.deleted_at is null
mutations.because: Dropping the tombstone filter lets a deleted org's member row satisfy the query, so memberTenant answers that org instead of undefined. The witness test seeds a user whose only org is deleted and asserts undefined with and without an active id; under this mutant the tenant is the deleted org and the toEqual/toBeUndefined assertion fails.
command: memberTenant answers undefined when the only org of the user is deleted

mutations.before: where m.user_id = $1 and o.deleted_at is null
mutations.because: Same defect witnessed through the tenant middleware: a member of a deleted org would resolve a tenant and reach the protected route. The witness test posts a session scoped to the deleted org and asserts 403 no_membership with the handler's body absent; under this mutant the route answers 200 and the status/body assertion fails.
command: a member of a deleted org is 403 no_membership and the route never runs

mutations.before: join org o on o.id = m.org_id
mutations.because: A join that is always true no longer excludes the deleted org's row, so a deleted active org resolves for a member of one deleted and two live orgs. The witness test asserts orgId is the first live org by id (beta); under this mutant it resolves to the deleted alpha and the assertion fails.
command: memberTenant skips a deleted active org and answers the first live org by id

mutations.because: Reversing the fallback order makes the highest-sorted live org win instead of the lowest, so a skipped deleted active org resolves to gamma rather than beta. The witness test asserts orgId is beta; under this mutant it is gamma and the assertion fails.
command: memberTenant skips a deleted active org and answers the first live org by id

mutations.before: alter table org add column deleted_at timestamptz;
mutations.after: alter table org add column deleted_at timestamptz default now();
mutations.because: A default of now() backfills every existing org as deleted at migration time, defeating the null-means-live invariant. The witness test asserts column_default is null and that every org still reads null after the migration; under this mutant column_default is now() and the shape assertion fails.
command: org deleted_at migration adds a nullable timestamptz column with no default

mutations.before: alter table org add column deleted_at timestamptz;
mutations.after: alter table org add column deleted_at timestamp;
mutations.because: Dropping the time zone from the column changes its data_type from 'timestamp with time zone' to 'timestamp without time zone'. The witness test asserts the exact data_type; under this mutant the shape assertion fails.
command: org deleted_at migration adds a nullable timestamptz column with no default
